newsitem.title: CHAD: President's party leads race for Chad parliament.
newsitem.headline: President's party leads race for Chad parliament.

text.p: President Idriss Deby's ruling party has a clear lead in the race for control of Chad's new 125-seat national assembly, final results from the January 5 first round of its legislative election showed on Saturday.
The results, released by the appeal court, credited Deby's Patriotic Salvation Movement with 37 seats against a total of 20 for various other parties.

A total of 68 seats will be contested in the second round, which was originally scheduled for February 23. Sources close to the independent national electoral commission say Deby will set the definitive date in a presidential decree.

The appeal court ordered a second round in six seats where provisional results showed Deby supporters winning in the first round. It scrapped the nomad vote -- an object of opposition allegations of vote rigging -- in all but three constituencies.

Deby, a former northern guerrilla leader, seized power in a 1990 French-backed coup. After repeated electoral delays, he won a multi-party presidential election in July in a runoff against southern rival and fellow general Wadal Abdelkader Kamougue.

Foreign Minister Saleh Kebzabo's National Union for Development and Renewal is second in the race for parliament with seven seats. Kamougue's party had four, the party of former transitional parliament speaker, Lol Mahamat Choua, three.
A total of 658 candidates from 49 parties contested the elections wrapping up the former French colony's transition to democracy after decades of internal strife or war with Libya.
International and national election monitors gave first-round polling a clean bill of health, despite complaints of minor irregularities and organisational problems.
